target: Ça ne casse pas trois pattes à un canard.
english: It's no big deal.
tip: 'Ne pas casser trois pattes à un canard' = 'nothing to write home about'.

target: Avoir d'autres chats à fouetter.
english: To have other fish to fry.
tip: 'Avoir d'autres chats à fouetter' = 'to have other things to do'.

target: Il m'a raconté des salades.
english: He told me a bunch of lies.
tip: 'Raconter des salades' = to tell lies/stories. Informal and humorous expression.

target: Avoir un chat dans la gorge.
english: To have a cat in one's throat.
tip: French: 'cat in the throat'. English: 'frog in the throat'.

target: C'est bonnet blanc et blanc bonnet.
english: It's six of one, half a dozen of the other.
tip: Same thing said differently. 'White hat and hat white'.

target: On se fait un ciné ce soir ?
english: Shall we go to the movies tonight?
tip: Familier: 'se faire un ciné' = 'to go see a movie'.

target: Je me permets de vous adresser ma candidature.
english: I take the liberty of sending you my application.
tip: Formal job application language. Soutenu register.

target: Daignez accepter mes humbles excuses.
english: Deign to accept my humble apologies.
tip: Très soutenu: 'daigner' = 'to deign'. Very formal apology.

target: Souffrez que je vous interrompe un instant.
english: Permit me to interrupt you for a moment.
tip: Très soutenu: 'souffrir' in sense of 'to permit'. Literary/archaic.

target: À l'attention de Monsieur le Directeur des Ressources Humaines.
english: For the attention of the Director of Human Resources.
tip: French has distinct registers: soutenu (formal), courant (standard), familier (informal), argot (slang).

target: Conformément à la réglementation en vigueur, nous vous informons que...
english: In accordance with the regulations in force, we inform you that...
tip: 'Conformément à' = in accordance with. Legal/official register for referencing regulations.

target: Par la présente, je vous informe de ma décision de démissionner.
english: I hereby inform you of my decision to resign.
tip: Soutenu: 'par la présente' = 'hereby'. Formal notification.

target: Dans l'attente de votre réponse, je vous prie de croire en l'assurance de ma considération.
english: Awaiting your reply, I assure you of my highest regards.
tip: 'N'hésitez pas à' = don't hesitate to. Standard business politeness formula.

target: Tenir la chandelle.
english: To be the third wheel.
tip: 'Tenir la chandelle' = 'to hold the candle'. Unwanted chaperone.

target: Il tombe des hallebardes.
english: It's pouring rain.
tip: 'Il tombe des hallebardes' = 'it's raining halberds'. Archaic but used.

target: Mettre les bouchées doubles.
english: To work twice as hard.
tip: 'Mettre les bouchées doubles' = 'to double one's efforts'.

target: Ce travail, c'est du gâteau.
english: This job is a piece of cake.
tip: 'C'est du gâteau' = it's a piece of cake. Same metaphor in both languages.

target: Il a vendu la mèche.
english: He let the cat out of the bag.
tip: 'Vendre la mèche' = 'to spill the beans/reveal a secret'.

target: Il est tombé dans le panneau.
english: He fell for the trick.
tip: 'Tomber dans le panneau' = 'to be tricked/fall for it'.

target: C'est une autre paire de manches.
english: That's a whole different story.
tip: 'Une autre paire de manches' = 'a different matter entirely'.

target: Elle a le cœur sur la main.
english: She's very generous.
tip: 'Avoir le cœur sur la main' = 'to be open-handed/generous'.

target: Il a tiré son épingle du jeu.
english: He got out of it well.
tip: 'Tirer son épingle du jeu' = 'to extricate oneself skilfully'.

target: Il a mis les pieds dans le plat.
english: He put his foot in it.
tip: 'Mettre les pieds dans le plat' = 'to be blunt/tactless'.

target: Ce sont eux qui ont pris cette décision, non pas nous.
english: It's they who made this decision, not us.
tip: Cleft sentence with 'ce sont...qui' for plural emphasis.

target: Il pleut des cordes.
english: It's raining cats and dogs.
tip: 'Des' = some (partitive plural). French requires it where English uses no article: 'des enfants' = children.

target: Il a mangé son chapeau.
english: He ate his hat.
tip: 'Manger son chapeau' = to eat one's words/hat. Used when proven wrong.

target: Remettre les pendules à l'heure.
english: To set the record straight.
tip: 'Remettre les pendules à l'heure' = 'to set things straight'.

target: Elle a une mémoire d'éléphant.
english: She has a memory like an elephant.
tip: 'Mémoire d'éléphant' = excellent memory. The elephant metaphor exists in both French and English.

target: Se noyer dans un verre d'eau.
english: To make a big fuss over something trivial.
tip: 'Se noyer dans un verre d'eau' = 'to drown in a glass of water'.

target: Elle a un poil dans la main.
english: She's extremely lazy.
tip: 'Avoir un poil dans la main' = 'to be very lazy'. Literal: 'hair in the hand'.

target: Il n'a pas la langue dans sa poche.
english: He's never at a loss for words.
tip: 'Ne pas avoir la langue dans sa poche' = 'to be outspoken'.

target: Si grand que soit le défi, nous le relèverons.
english: However great the challenge may be, we will take it on.
tip: Si + adj + que + subjunctive: concessive inversion.

target: Ce sur quoi nous devons nous concentrer, c'est la qualité.
english: What we need to focus on is quality.
tip: 'Ce sur quoi' = what...on/about. Preposition + quoi for things: 'ce à quoi', 'ce pour quoi'.

target: Se regarder le nombril.
english: To be navel-gazing.
tip: 'Se regarder le nombril' = 'to be navel-gazing/self-absorbed'.

target: Le soldat tomba au champ d'honneur.
english: The soldier fell on the field of honour.
tip: 'Tomba' – passé simple of tomber. In literature, even 'être' verbs use passé simple (not passé composé).

target: Ceux dont les dossiers sont incomplets doivent se présenter demain.
english: Those whose files are incomplete must come in tomorrow.
tip: 'Ceux dont' = those whose/of whom. 'Ceux' is the demonstrative pronoun for masculine plural.

target: Ainsi va la vie.
english: Such is life.
tip: 'Ainsi' at start of sentence can trigger inversion: 'Ainsi va la vie' = Such is life.

target: Peut-être aurait-il dû réfléchir davantage.
english: Perhaps he should have thought more.
tip: 'Peut-être' + inversion: 'peut-être aurait-il dû'. In formal register, 'peut-être' at start triggers inversion.

target: C'est ce dont je me doutais.
english: That's what I suspected.
tip: 'Ce dont' = 'that of which/what'. Replaces 'de + ce que'.

target: Aussi étonnant que cela paraisse, c'est la vérité.
english: As surprising as it may seem, it's the truth.
tip: 'Aussi' at start of sentence + inversion means 'therefore/so' (literary). Not 'also' in this position.

target: À peine fut-il sorti qu'il se mit à pleuvoir.
english: He had barely gone out when it started to rain.
tip: 'À peine fut-il sorti que' – passé simple with inversion in literary narrative. Passé antérieur before main event.

target: Dès que le silence se fut installé, il prit la parole.
english: As soon as silence had fallen, he began to speak.
tip: 'Voir' in passé simple: je vis, il vit, nous vîmes, ils virent.

target: C'est là que le bât blesse.
english: That's where the shoe pinches.
tip: 'Le bât blesse' = 'the packsaddle hurts'. Where the problem lies.

target: C'est ce en quoi je crois fermement.
english: That's what I firmly believe in.
tip: 'Ce en quoi': preposition + quoi after 'croire en'.

target: Ils vécurent heureux et eurent beaucoup d'enfants.
english: They lived happily and had many children.
tip: Classic fairy tale ending. Passé simple of vivre: vécurent.

target: Aussitôt qu'il eut prononcé ces mots, un silence tomba.
english: As soon as he had spoken these words, silence fell.
tip: 'Eut prononcé' – passé antérieur of prononcer. Used after 'aussitôt que/dès que' in literary texts.

target: Rares sont les occasions de le rencontrer.
english: Opportunities to meet him are rare.
tip: Inverted structure for emphasis: adjective before verb.

target: La manière dont il a réagi est inacceptable.
english: The way he reacted is unacceptable.
tip: 'Dont' replaces 'de': 'la manière dont il a réagi' = the way in which he reacted (réagir de cette manière).

target: Sitôt qu'il eut achevé sa tâche, il s'endormit.
english: The moment he had finished his task, he fell asleep.
tip: 'Être' in passé simple: je fus, tu fus, il fut, nous fûmes, vous fûtes, ils furent.

target: Le roi convoqua ses ministres et leur fit part de sa décision.
english: The king summoned his ministers and informed them of his decision.
tip: 'Convoqua' – passé simple of convoquer (-er verbs: -ai, -as, -a, -âmes, -âtes, -èrent).

target: Après qu'elle eut pleuré, elle se ressaisit.
english: After she had cried, she pulled herself together.
tip: The passé antérieur replaces the plus-que-parfait in literary texts after time conjunctions.

target: Pierre qui roule n'amasse pas mousse.
english: A rolling stone gathers no moss.
tip: French proverb matching English 'A rolling stone gathers no moss'. Same metaphor, different language.

target: Elle résolut de ne plus jamais mentir.
english: She resolved never to lie again.
tip: Passé simple of résoudre: résolut. Rare and literary.

target: Les résultats obtenus invitent à la prudence.
english: The results obtained call for caution.
tip: 'Force est de constater' = one must acknowledge. Impersonal obligation to recognize a fact.

target: Un tiens vaut mieux que deux tu l'auras.
english: A bird in the hand is worth two in the bush.
tip: 'Tel père, tel fils' = like father, like son. 'Tel' = such/like, agrees with the noun.

target: Les travaux antérieurs n'ont pas suffisamment pris en compte ce facteur.
english: Previous works have not sufficiently taken this factor into account.
tip: 'Les travaux antérieurs' = previous works/studies. Standard academic reference to prior research.

target: Force est de constater que les résultats sont insuffisants.
english: We are forced to note that the results are insufficient.
tip: Force est de + infinitive: formal acknowledgment structure.

target: Cherchez la femme.
english: Look for the woman.
tip: Expression suggesting a woman is often behind events. From Dumas.

target: Mieux vaut tard que jamais.
english: Better late than never.
tip: 'Mieux vaut' = it is better. Impersonal construction: 'mieux vaut tard que jamais'.

target: Il n'est de pire eau que l'eau qui dort.
english: Still waters are the most dangerous.
tip: Proverb about hidden dangers in quiet appearances.
